newsitem.title: PERU: Peru 28-day CDs draw 12.41 pct avg rate at sale.
newsitem.headline: Peru 28-day CDs draw 12.41 pct avg rate at sale.

text.p: The Central Reserve Bank of Peru said Tuesday it accepted bids for 28-day Certificates of Deposit (CDs) worth 45 million soles at an effective average annual rate of 12.41 percent during a bank auction.
The CDs have a June 11 starting date.
The accepted bids also had a minimum rate of 12.10 percent and a maximum rate of 12.50 percent, the bank said.
At the last CD auction June 5, 28-day CDs drew an average rate of 12.70 percent. At Tuesday's auction, the bank said it received bids on the CDs totalling 105.8 million soles.
The bank had offered 45.0 million soles worth of CDs.

Last year the bank regularly held auctions on Tuesdays and Thursdays but has limited its sales in 1997 due to a lack of liquidity in the financial system. Until last Thursday, the bank had not held a CD auction for two months.
The average effective annual interest rate for the certificates is used as an informal indicator for interest rates in the Peruvian financial system.
